title: P0: Hosted API — Edge protocol upgrade fallback flood postmortem (2026-10-21)
content:
Summary:

On 2026-10-21 at ~08:14 UTC we observed a P0 degradation of the Hosted API: streaming sessions were intermittently failing with resets and a sustained increase in 5xx rates and tail latency for ~51 minutes. Impacted traffic was primarily streaming (SSE/HTTP2) through a subset of edge nodes which had received a new protocol-handling configuration intended to improve multiplexing performance. The configuration caused degraded behavior on mixed-version edge clusters which led to connection resets, aggressive client retries, and a transient overload of the request-routing/control-plane components.

Why this matters:
- Customer-facing streaming degraded: many customers saw partial responses, reconnect loops, and non-idempotent retry behavior.
- P95/P99 token-serving latency rose, increasing cost and SLO violations for several customers.
- Incident was P0 due to broad customer impact and severity of errors (5xx surge).

Incident window:
- 08:11 UTC — Pre-rollout monitoring green; runtime canary scheduled.
- 08:14 UTC — Canary completed and rollout started to 20% of edge nodes (automated).
- 08:20 UTC — First alerts: p99 streaming latency increase and a spike in tcp resets on canary hosts.
- 08:24 UTC — Error rate for streaming endpoints rose from baseline ~0.3% to 22% in affected regions.
- 08:28 UTC — Oncall paged; SREs triaging in #sre-incident-2026-10-21.
- 08:34 UTC — Initial mitigation: paused rollout via orchestration system; however, partial rollout already hit many regional edge rings and some nodes continued to accept traffic.
- 08:40 UTC — Root-cause hypothesis formed: protocol-handling change caused some older proxy instances to reject frames -> TCP resets -> client reconnect storm.
- 08:45 UTC — Emergency rollback started for the feature flag/config on all edge nodes.
- 08:56 UTC — Rollback propagation completed for 95% of nodes; 5xx/latency started trending down.
- 09:05 UTC — Incident declared resolved for most customers; follow-up monitoring kept for next 24 hours.

Impact:
- ~18–25% of streaming sessions in affected regions saw immediate resets during the window.
- Aggregated 5xx rate for hosted-api increased to a peak of ~22% for streaming endpoints; non-streaming endpoints were hit less heavily (5–8% increases).
- P99 latency for tokenized routing climbed from ~420ms to ~3.2s on impacted paths.
- Estimated customer-facing minutes impacted: ~13k minutes cumulatively across accounts.

Root cause (short):
A protocol-handling configuration intended to enable an experimental multiplex/frame-handling optimization was rolled out to a portion of the edge fleet. The config changed the behavior of how SPDY/HTTP2 frames with a custom SETTINGS flag and header compression were negotiated. Mixed-version edge nodes (new config + older proxy versions) occasionally failed to interpret the SETTINGS handshake, causing them to close connections with a TCP RST. SDKs and client libraries lacked a sufficiently backoff-aware reconnect policy and immediately attempted aggressive reconnects, creating a fan-out of ephemeral sessions. This sudden connection growth caused control-plane KV lease contention and connection table pressure on backends, which produced 5xx errors and increased tail latency.

Contributing factors (detailed):
- Rollout process: automated rollout allowed the config to progress beyond a small canary quickly; health-check gating didn't catch the specific frame-rejection pattern because our canary traffic skew didn't include high-percent streaming loads.
- Backwards-compatibility: the new SETTINGS flag/handling was not fully compatible with older proxy builds; feature gate lacked strict version compatibility checks.
- Telemetry gaps: no dedicated metric for "frame-reject-rate" or "settings-negotiation-failure", so triage required correlating tcp resets, handshake logs, and 5xx spikes across multiple components.
- Client behavior: several popular SDKs used by customers retry aggressively without exponential backoff/jitter for streaming session failures, amplifying the reconnect flood.
- Runbook coverage: our protocol-upgrade runbook didn't have a play for "partial handshake failures causing client-retry storms"; oncall had to improvise throttling steps.

Immediate mitigations performed during the incident:
- Paused and then rolled back the edge config/feature flag across the fleet (08:45–08:56 UTC).
- Applied short-term connection-rate caps at the edge to slow the reconnect flood while rollback propagated.
- Enabled a temporary per-IP token bucket limiter for new streaming session creation on affected rings.
- Increased visibility: enabled detailed handshake logging on a small subset of nodes for forensic capture.
- Communicated to customers via status page and #customer-commms draft; engineering-led customer outreach for top-tier accounts.

Longer-term remediation (action items):
1) Deployment & rollout process tightening (owner: Diego Martins, due: 2026-11-05) — require staged rollouts with explicit version-compatibility checks and block rollout if frame-negotiation failures > 0.1% in canary traffic for 30m. Add a rolling canary process that routes a fixed fraction of high-streaming-load traffic to canary nodes.
2) Feature gate/version check (owner: Rina Chowdhury, due: 2026-11-12) — add explicit edge-proxy-min-version enforcement for protocol changes; orchestration must refuse to apply new SETTINGS flags to older nodes.
3) Telemetry augmentation (owner: Liam O'Connor, due: 2026-11-02) — add metrics: settings_negotiation_failures, frame_reject_rate, per-node handshake_failure_rate; surface in SLO dashboards and create alert with clear thresholds.
4) SDK client guidance (owner: Evelyn Nguyen, due: 2026-11-16) — publish guidance and patch releases for official SDKs to implement exponential backoff + jitter for streaming reconnect, and add client-side circuit breaker docs.
5) Runbook update & playbook addition (owner: Aisha Patel, due: 2026-10-29) — write explicit "protocol-upgrade-fallback-flood" runbook section with triage steps, throttles, and automatic rollback checklist.
6) Orchestration safety nets (owner: Platform Eng, TBD) — consider an automated global rollback if cross-region handshake errors exceed X in Y minutes; implement an automated pause and alert.

Changes already committed (post-incident):
- Full rollback of config completed and verified (08:56 UTC).
- Short-term per-node connection limiter added as a guard until SDK changes roll out.
- New logging capture job (ephemeral) saved handshake traces to S3 for the investigation (ticket SRE-1842-a11).

Runbook & process updates proposed:
- Add "protocol negotiation" health checks to canary traffic: canary generators must exercise streaming handshake edge cases (headers, SETTINGS flags, header compression variations).
- Make canary duration configurable with a minimum of 60 minutes for protocol-impacting changes.
- Require a sign-off from the edge-proxy compatibility owner before enabling non-backwards-compatible SETTINGS.

Lessons learned (short bullets):
- Even small protocol/handshake tweaks can have outsized systemic impact when mixed-version fleets exist.
- Canary traffic composition must match production traffic profiles (streaming vs short-lived requests).
- Client-side retry policies matter: server-side failures are frequently amplified by unthrottled client retries.
- Metrics specific to handshake/negotiation failures are essential for fast detection.

Follow-ups & verification plan:
- Verify SDKs have backoff changes in canary via internal integration tests (Evelyn, due 2026-11-02).
- Add metric and alert, then run a tabletop incident drill in December focused on protocol-upgrade failures (Diego, due 2026-12-10).
- Validate orchestration enforces min-version before applying flags in a staging run (Rina, due 2026-11-09).

Open questions:
- Should we add server-side passive client-rate-limiting as a permanent guard for streaming endpoints? Pros/cons and cost impact need evaluation.
- What is an appropriate global threshold for triggering an automated rollback for protocol-negotiation errors across regions?

Postmortem sign-off:
- Owner: Aisha Patel (eng-sre)
- Reviewers: Diego Martins (site-reliability), Rina Chowdhury (platform), Evelyn Nguyen (SDK), Liam O'Connor (observability)

Appendix: useful traces & quick refs
- Packet-level example of malformed SETTINGS negotiation (saved under S3: s3://redwood-incident-logs/2026-10-21/handshake-dumps.tar.gz)
- Incident Slack thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/CSRE12345/p1666425600000
- Jira ticket: SRE-1842 (parent), SRE-1842-a11 (logging capture), SRE-1842-fix (feature-gate enforcement)

Notes to self / informal:
- We got lucky that the rollback automation worked fast; if rollback had been slower by even 10 minutes the reconnect storm would likely have knocked down more downstream services.
- Make sure to include SDK maintainers in the tabletop next time — client behavior is part of the system.
